intro: This branch is about shapes and space: naming flat and solid shapes, noticing their features, fitting shapes together, and describing where things are. It also brings the first taste of fractions through halves and quarters.

I.6.01.what: Naming common flat shapes such as circles, squares, rectangles and triangles.

levels.a: Recognizes a circle and tells it apart from similar shapes like an oval.
levels.b: Tells a square (four equal sides) from a rectangle.
levels.d: Names less common shapes: hexagon (6 sides), rhombus (a slanted square) and trapezoid.

I.6.02.what: Describing flat shapes by their features: how many sides and corners, and whether the sides are straight or curved.

levels.a: Counts the sides of a shape.
levels.b: Counts the corners, where two sides meet.
levels.c: Says whether a shape's sides are straight, curved or both.
levels.d: Counts both sides and corners, noticing the numbers match.
levels.e: Adds up the corners of several triangles and squares.
levels.f: Solves a puzzle: from the number of shapes and total sides, finds how many are squares.

I.6.03.what: Recognizing a shape whichever way it is turned or stretched, by focusing on what makes it that shape.

levels.a: Decides whether a tilted four-sided shape really is a square.
levels.b: Recognizes tall, thin or turned triangles as triangles.
levels.c: Rejects look-alikes with a gap or a curved side.
levels.d: Explains what makes a shape a triangle, whatever its color, size or direction.

I.6.04.what: Naming common solid (3D) shapes such as cubes, spheres, cones and cylinders.

levels.a: Recognizes a cube, shaped like a dice.
levels.b: Recognizes a sphere, round all over like a ball.
levels.c: Recognizes a cone and a cylinder (a can shape).
levels.d: Recognizes a box shape, called a rectangular prism.

I.6.05.what: Describing solid shapes: how they move and what flat faces they have.

levels.a: Says whether a solid can roll, stack or slide.
levels.b: Counts the flat faces (surfaces) on a solid, including hidden ones.
levels.c: Names the flat shape of a face, like the square face of a cube.
levels.d: Matches everyday objects to solid shapes, like an ice cube to a cube.

I.6.06.what: Combining smaller shapes to make bigger ones, like two triangles making a square.

levels.a: Says what shape two triangles make when put together.
levels.b: Works out how many small blocks cover a bigger shape.
levels.c: Chooses blocks that fill an outline exactly, with no gaps.
levels.d: Finds more than one set of blocks that makes the same shape.

I.6.07.what: Breaking a shape into smaller shapes, and seeing the smaller shapes hidden inside a picture.

levels.a: Says what shapes you get when a square is cut along a line.
levels.b: Finds which smaller shapes make up a bigger one.
levels.c: Counts the small triangles inside a picture.
levels.d: Works out which shape the pieces make when pushed back together.
levels.e: Counts every rectangle in a picture, big and small, including ones made of smaller pieces.
levels.f: Counts every triangle, big and small, in a triangle crossed by lines.

I.6.08.what: Building and describing structures made from cubes and other solid blocks.

levels.a: Counts the blocks in a simple tower.
levels.b: Picks the building that matches a model exactly.
levels.c: Works out which blocks were used to build a pictured tower.
levels.d: Counts all the cubes in a larger building, column by column.

I.6.09.what: Using position words like above, below, between, behind and left to describe where things are.

levels.c: Uses in front of and behind.
levels.d: Uses left and right, as seen from where the learner is looking.

I.6.10.what: Following and giving directions to move a character around a grid of squares.

levels.a: Counts steps forward or back to reach a target.
levels.b: Turns left or right from the character's own point of view.
levels.c: Finds the shortest route to a target, going around obstacles.
levels.d: Chooses the directions, like "4 right, then 1 up," that reach the target.
levels.e: Works out the moves that take the robot back to where it started.
levels.f: Follows a long list of moves and works out how far right of the start the robot ends.

I.6.11.what: Understanding halves: two equal parts of a shape or a group.

levels.a: Decides whether two parts are equal in size.
levels.b: Picks out the shape that is cut into halves.
levels.c: Finds half of a small group by sharing it into two equal groups.
levels.d: Spots shapes cut into two parts that are not halves because they are unequal.

I.6.12.what: Understanding quarters: four equal parts, each one half of a half.

levels.a: Names the shaded part of a shape as a half or a quarter.
levels.b: Picks out the shape cut into four equal parts.
levels.c: Finds a quarter of a small group by sharing it into four equal groups.
levels.d: Knows a half of a shape is bigger than a quarter of the same shape.
levels.e: Works backwards from a quarter to find a half or the whole amount.
levels.f: Solves stories with a half of a half, working back to the starting amount.

I.6.13.what: Understanding symmetry: a shape is symmetrical if it can be folded so the two halves match exactly.

levels.a: Decides whether two sides match when folded along a line.
levels.b: Picks the fold line (line of symmetry) that splits a shape into matching halves.
levels.c: Completes a picture by drawing its mirror-image half.
levels.d: Finds symmetry in everyday things like letters and numbers.

I.6.14.what: Solving riddles that describe a shape by its features, like "I have 3 corners."

levels.a: Guesses a shape from one clue about its features.
levels.b: Uses two clues together to pin down the shape.
levels.c: Chooses which riddle describes a given shape.
levels.d: Checks a set of shapes against a riddle and counts how many fit.
